mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% annually signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations contract under higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized rate exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved economic growth prospects.
failure_condition: The joint effect of UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the interaction term's coefficient in a regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high housing starts (HOUST) and strong consumer spending (RSAFS), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as the economy approaches a peak and the risk of a downturn increases, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 850 and RSAFS > 400000, or the regime-specific Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100) indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate profits and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 100, or the Rank IC over a 1-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% within a 3-month period signals an emerging labor market weakness that reduces consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized growth rate signals robust economic activity, which typically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through improved corporate earnings and investor confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 annualized growth exceeds 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% annually signals disinflation, which may lead to a prolonged period of accommodative monetary policy and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate rate cuts and lower real interest rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized rate falls below 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
